cases.prompt: Find architecture examples for a workflow scheduler with DAG execution and retry semantics.

baseline.provenance: deterministic baseline fixture representing a generic answer without repository search or local code-card evidence
baseline.output: Consider using a DAG abstraction with nodes, edges, retries, and a worker queue. You may want a scheduler loop, persistent task state, and retry policies. A database table can track task status. Consider adding observability and backoff.

repomind.provenance: deterministic RepoMind fixture assembled from recorded local code-card fields: repository URL, source paths, architecture summary, and transfer notes
repomind.output: RepoMind result: https://github.com/apache/airflow shows a mature workflow DAG scheduler. Code locations: airflow/models/dag.py, airflow/jobs/scheduler_job_runner.py, airflow/models/taskinstance.py. Why useful: it separates DAG definition, scheduling decisions, and task instance state, which directly maps to retry semantics and executor handoff. Implementation guidance: model the DAG as immutable workflow metadata, persist each task attempt separately, and keep scheduler decisions idempotent so crashed scheduler loops can resume safely.

baseline.provenance: deterministic baseline fixture representing a generic answer without repository search or local code-card evidence
baseline.output: Consider defining a plugin interface with lifecycle hooks and configuration. Modules should be isolated from the core app. You can load plugins dynamically and expose extension points. Consider documenting the API clearly.

repomind.output: RepoMind result: https://github.com/prettier/prettier demonstrates an extensible formatter plugin boundary. Code locations: src/main/core.js, src/main/parser-and-printer.js, docs/plugins.md. Why useful: the core separates orchestration from plugin-provided parser/printer modules while preserving centralized option handling. Implementation guidance: keep the host responsible for orchestration and errors, make each module boundary explicit, and version the boundary so third-party plugins can survive internal refactors.

cases.prompt: Find data ingestion pipeline architecture examples with queueing, batching, and failure recovery.

baseline.provenance: deterministic baseline fixture representing a generic answer without repository search or local code-card evidence
baseline.output: Consider putting messages on a queue, processing them in batches, and retrying failures. Store offsets or checkpoints. Use dead-letter queues for poison messages and add metrics. The design should separate ingestion from processing.

repomind.output: RepoMind result: https://github.com/apache/beam shows a portable data ingestion pipeline model for batching, queue-like bundle execution, and recovery.
